# Halloween: mansion interior

Select `HauntedInteriorLoop` in the Studio. The preset `presets/halloween-haunted-interior.json` creates a **16-second, 1920×1080, 60 fps** loop in MP4/WebM, meant as a stream background. The initial values are `seed: 113`, `backgroundColor: #080D10` and a palette of grey-green, pale moonlight and amber. The scene is drawn in SVG, with no text, external images, extra fonts or audio.

The hall is seen in central perspective, with a single vanishing point at the center of the frame (960, 540). The room is modeled in meters and projected by a single camera. Skirting, wainscot, frieze and cornice wrap the corners without seams. Floor joints, ceiling, windows and curtains recede to the same point, and the spacing shortens with depth.

The content area is the **1100×620 pixel** rectangle centered in the frame (x from 410 to 1510, y from 230 to 850). The back wall takes exactly that area: a camera or game capture placed there sits embedded in the room. Ceiling, floor and side walls form the frame around it, and the room's corners follow the frame's diagonals. Without a capture, the wall shows a large dark arch leading to a gloomy corridor, and the central band (x from 610 to 1310, y from 400 to 650) sits entirely over that opening, calm for titles. Nothing moves inside the content area, in any frame and with any seed.

The hierarchy runs from the center to the edges. The candles are the main light: two floor candelabra at the bottom corners warm the wall, the velvet and the floor, and a ring chandelier hangs from the ceiling above the content area, without entering it. The moonlight is the cold counterpoint: each side wall has a pointed window with crimson velvet curtains, and there is a single moon, low, outside the right wall, the same one that lights the open door and the corridor's stairs. Through the right window, it casts the window's shape on the floor, with the shadows of the mullion, the transoms and the tracery, stretched diagonally from the foot of the wall. Away from the window, the edges soften and the light weakens; a soft beam links the glass to the floor and fades before the content area. The left window faces away from the moon: the glass shows the night sky, dimmer, and only a faint diffuse glow reaches the floor along the wall. Portraits, damask, cracks and cobwebs stay in the background, in low contrast.

The chandelier sways gently, the flames and the candlelight vary, the moonlight breathes, the portraits' eyes appear now and then, the fog moves along the floor and the dust floats in the side bands. Motion and lighting depend only on the frame, the parameters and the seed, with continuous position and speed at the loop seam.

Outside, lightning strikes, one in each window, at moments chosen by the seed and away from the loop seam. Each has a quick flash, a second flash 150–250 ms later and a tail that fades within 0.8 s. The bolt shows only in the window facing it, behind the leading, the trees and the stone tracery. Both windows light up together, the bolt's one more strongly. On the bolt's side, the flash lights the wall around the lancet, the edge of the candelabrum facing the window and a wide, soft glow on the floor, without the shape of the frames, because the bolt and the lit clouds are a large light source, not a point like the moon. The moonlight pool does not brighten with the flash. All of this stays outside the content area. Cycles of 3 seconds or more have two lightning strikes; from 1.5 to 3 seconds, one; below 1.5 seconds, none. At least 1.5 seconds pass between the start of two strikes, so no second has more than two flashes.

`colors[0]` controls fog and atmosphere, `colors[1]` the moonlight, the glass and the dust, and `colors[2]` the candles. With only two colors, the candles take the first. `dustCount: 0` removes the dust; `fogIntensity: 0` removes the fog. `candleIntensity` adjusts the light of the candles and the chandelier, `moonlightIntensity` the strength of the moonlight in the right window (and of the diffuse glow on the left), `hauntingIntensity` the appearance of the eyes in the portraits, `chandelierSway` the amplitude of the chandelier's sway and `lightningIntensity` the strength of the lightning (default 0.7; `0` turns the flashes off). Intensities and sway range from 0 to 1; `dustCount` takes integers from 0 to 100. The controls can be saved in the Studio with **Save default props**.

With `transparent: true` and `outputFormat: "webm"`, the room opens over the game. The back wall, the arch, the central floor field, the ceiling and the vignette disappear. The side walls with windows, curtains and portraits remain, with the floor strips along them holding the candelabra, and the chandelier, which now hangs from the top edge by its chain. The kept pieces are opaque, without transparency ramps. Glows, fog and dust sit over them, and the cuts have a dark finish. The moonlight reflection on the floor goes with the central field, and the lightning flash is painted only in the core of the kept pieces, without changing the alpha. The content area is fully transparent. In MP4/GIF, the scene is composited over `backgroundColor`. To export the preset as MP4, use `npm run render:mp4 -- HauntedInteriorLoop --props presets/halloween-haunted-interior.json`; switch to `render:webm` or `render:gif` for the other formats, keeping the official profiles in [Formats](../export.md#formats).

## Overlay kit

The [`halloween-haunted-interior`](../overlays.md#themes) theme dresses chat, blocks and borders for this background, with the same 16 s and seed 113: `presets/chat-halloween-haunted-interior.json`, `presets/block-halloween-haunted-interior.json` and `presets/border-halloween-haunted-interior.json`, and the pack comes out with `npm run render:pack -- halloween-haunted-interior`. The `haunted-interior` ornaments bring the hall's brass, candles and velvet: candelabra with the same flame and the same flicker as the background's candles, two-candle sconces and velvet valances with tassels. The presets turn `lightning` on, and with the same seed and duration the lightning strikes at the same instants as the background: panels, frames and candelabra light up together with the hall's windows, more strongly on the bolt's side. In OBS, a media source restarts from the beginning when the scene becomes active again (if the restart-on-activate option is on, the default); so the overlays only flash together with the background when they start together: put the background and the overlays in the same scene, with the same option. The ornaments live in the bleed, so leave about 48 px free around the webcams (72 px on `webcam-16x9-lg` and 96 px on `gameplay`, where the ornaments are enlarged) and 32 px around the chat and the blocks, including up to the screen edge and between one piece and the next; in particular, leave at least 96 px between the game frame and the screen edge, so the candles are not cut. See also [Halloween kits](../kits-halloween.md).
